paper_id: Qian et al. - 2018 - Enabling Contactless Detection of Moving Humans with Dynamic Speeds Using CSI
title: Enabling Contactless Detection of Moving Humans with Dynamic Speeds Using CSI
motivation: RSS-based detection suffers from coarse granularity; existing CSI methods ignore phase and cannot handle dynamic walking speeds
problem_framing: Extract sensitive features from full CSI (amplitude+phase) using eigenvalue-based correlation matrices and multi-antenna diversity
key_insight: Phase difference across antennas has higher variance than linear transformation, yielding better sensitivity to human motion
method_signature: Phase difference + outlier filtering → correlation matrix eigenvalues → SVM classification for motion detection
evaluation_criteria: True-Positive rate (motion detection) and True-Negative rate (static environment classification)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: PADS cannot detect quasi-static humans; requires motion for detection; theoretical limitation acknowledged
evidence_for_taste: few of them have explored the full potential of CSI
phase difference tends to have higher variance
phase differences across antennas have clear physical meaning
major information of human motion centers upon the first three eigenvalues
gathering CSI data where humans walk at slow speeds is sufficient and necessary
thinking_moves: 先验证相位差异比线性变换相位方差更大, 再选择前者
从天线间距导致相位独立性角度解释方差差异
从特征工程角度统一振幅和相位特征表达
通过交叉验证发现慢速行走数据训练效果最佳
